title: Flapping Soft Fin Deformation Modeling using Planar Laser-Induced Fluorescence Imaging
protocol: Build a fin mold based on the desired shape design.
Design and build a custom 3D-printed gloss-finished mold of fin shape.
Insert structural elements into the mold, such as a 3D-printed rigid plastic leading-edge spar.
Mix PDMS in the desired part ratio to achieve higher or lower elastic modulus.
Weigh the corresponding amounts of base elastomer and curing agent.
Measure the fluorescent pigment so that the total mixture contains 0.1%-1% pigment by weight.
Add the pigment to the PDMS blend.
Pour the measured amounts of elastomer, hardener, and pigment into a planetary centrifugal mixer.
Mix at 423 x g for 30 seconds.
De-aerate at 465 x g for 30 seconds.
Degas and pour the PDMS mixture into the mold for the fin.
Place the mold into the oven at 70 °C for 45 minutes.
Let it cure overnight at 37 °C.
Once curing is complete, remove the cast fin from the mold.
Perform tensile testing following the ASTM standard.
Cast one Type IV specimen using the same PDMS and pigment blend in a Type IV shaped mold.
Clamp the test specimen into the tensile testing machine.
Measure the initial length, width, and thickness of the narrow sample section.
Subject the test specimen to tension in 5 mm increments within the elastic region only.
Decrease the tension in 5 mm increments until the total sample displacement returns to 0 mm (original position).
Record the lengths and forces at each increment.
Plot the stress-strain curve to calculate the elastic modulus of the sample.
Mount the PLIF hardware to a rectangular glass water tank (2.41 m x 0.76 m x 0.76 m).
Mount and use a pulsed laser system to generate a planar light sheet intersecting the tank at its mid-plane at 30 Hz.
Mount and use a 4 MP charge-coupled device camera equipped with a lens (35 mm) and a longpass fluorescence filter (560 nm).
Calibrate the micrometer-to-pixel conversion by taking an image from the CCD camera with a ruler placed in the laser sheet plane.
Select two positions on the camera and divide the distance in micrometers by separating pixels.
Synchronize the laser pulses and camera images with the flapping fin using trigger outputs from the fin software and signals from a delay generator.
Set the Trigger Source to EXT LAMP/EXT Q-SW (external lamp/external Q-switch).
For both laser heads, set the laser energy to the desired level (approximately 60%-80% of full power).
Ensure that the Q-switch is turned on by pressing each Q-switch button.
Turn the lasers on by pressing the Power button.
Plug in the power cables to the camera and ensure proper connections to the computer and software.
Open the camera settings software and select the proper port.
Set "Trigger in:" to External and "Mode:" to Fast under Trigger > Settings.
Set "Exposure Control" to Off under Exposure.
Select the proper camera card in the camera capture software.
Click on the Grab Sequence button.
Select TIFF images, Series of frames..., desired file path, 6 Digit Number, Continuous, and Accept in Capture Settings.
Click on Start Capture.
Turn on the delay generator.
Connect External Gate Channel to the fin trigger, Channels A-D to the laser (A: laser head 1, B: Q-switch to laser 1, C: laser head 2, D: Q-switch to laser 2), and Channel E to the camera.
Select "Pulse Mode" to Burst and "System Resolution" to 4 ns in delay generator software.
Set "Period (s)" to 0.033333352.
Set "External Trigger/Gate Mode" to Triggered, "Threshold (V)" to 0.20, and "Trigger Edge" as Rising.
Enable Channel A on the device.
Set the delay for Channel A to 0.000000004 seconds.
Set the width for Channel A to 0.005000000 seconds.
Set the amplitude for Channel A to 5.00 volts.
Set the channel mode for Channel A to Duty Cycle.
Set the wait count for Channel A to 0.
Set the sync source for Channel A to T0.
Set the polarity for Channel A to Normal.
Set the multiplexer setting for Channel A to A.
Set the duty cycle on and off times for Channel A to 1.
Disable the gate mode for Channel A.
Enable Channel B on the device.
Set the delay for Channel B to 0.000138000 seconds.
Set the width for Channel B to 0.005000000 seconds.
Set the amplitude for Channel B to 5.00 volts.
Set the channel mode for Channel B to Duty Cycle.
Set the wait count for Channel B to 0.
Set the sync source for Channel B to Ch A.
Set the polarity for Channel B to Normal.
Set the multiplexer setting for Channel B to B.
Set the duty cycle on and off times for Channel B to 1.
Disable the gate mode for Channel B.
Enable Channel C on the device.
Set the delay for Channel C to 0.033333304 seconds.
Set the width for Channel C to 0.005000000 seconds.
Set the amplitude for Channel C to 5.00 volts.
Set the channel mode for Channel C to Duty Cycle.
Set the wait count for Channel C to 0.
Set the sync source for Channel C to Ch A.
Set the polarity for Channel C to Normal.
Set the multiplexer setting for Channel C to C.
Set the duty cycle on and off times for Channel C to 1.
Disable the gate mode for Channel C.
Enable Channel D on the device.
Set the delay for Channel D to 0.000138000 seconds.
Set the width for Channel D to 0.005000000 seconds.
Set the amplitude for Channel D to 5.00 volts.
Set the channel mode for Channel D to Duty Cycle.
Set the wait count for Channel D to 0.
Set the sync source for Channel D to Ch C.
Set the polarity for Channel D to Normal.
Set the multiplexer setting for Channel D to D.
Set the duty cycle on and off times for Channel D to 1.
Disable the gate mode for Channel D.
Click on the Enabled checkbox under Channels > Ch E.
Set the "Delay (s)" to 0.000000004.
Set the "Width (s)" to 0.005000000.
Set the "Amplitude (V)" to 5.00.
Select "Channel Mode" as Normal.
Set the "Wait Count" to 0.
Choose "Sync Source" as T0.
Set the "Polarity" to Normal.
Select "Multiplexer" as E.
Set the "Gate Mode" to Disabled.
Align the fin so that the laser sheet passes through one chordwise section at a selected spanwise position.
Secure the fin platform with mounting hardware.
Connect power to the fin control hardware and fin motors.
Turn off all ambient lights.
Press Run in the delay generator software to begin synchronized experiments.
Acquire images of the intersection of the laser sheet with the fin throughout the stroke cycle for 200+ stroke cycles.
Press Stop in the delay generator software after completing data acquisition.
Disconnect the power source from the fin control hardware and motors.
Move the fin platform so that the laser sheet crosses at a new spanwise position.
Perform experiments again to acquire images at this new position.
Repeat Steps 2.3.-2.6 for eight different spanwise positions.
Replace the fin with additional desired stiffness membranes (PDMS 10:1 and PDMS 20:1).
Repeat the experiments with each new membrane.
Locate the file where the images are stored.
Create a subfolder for each fin position or phase throughout the stroke cycle.
Sort the image files into their corresponding subfolders.
Read 200+ images as pixel-value arrays (imread.m).
Sum the pixel-value arrays for all the images.
Divide by the number of images to generate a mean image.
Write the image to a new file (imwrite.m).
Repeat this step for each fin position throughout the stroke cycle (30 positions).
Perform histogram enhancement on each mean image (imadjust.m) to extend dynamic intensity range and improve contrast between the fin and background.
Set the intensity thresholds and binarize each image to obtain a black-and-white image (imbinarize.m).
Extract all white objects (fin pieces) from the binary image using bwareafilt.m.
Display the image using imshow.m.
Create a trace of the binary image boundary for each image to obtain a 2D shape by selecting all the fin (white) pixels that touch the background (black) pixels using bwboundaries.m.
Perform Steps 3.1.-3.5. for each fin cross-section.
Assume that the LE position in flexible cases is the same as that of the LE in a rigid fin of the same shape.
Line the plane cuts along their LE for the same time-step and compare with the results from the corresponding rigid fin shape.
Use a least-squares fit to approximate the resulting centerline shape of the fin cross-section for all plane cuts.
Reconstruct the 3D fin shape using a simplified convex-hull from these fitted profiles.
Compare the resulting fin shapes with 3D FSI models generated from their centerlines.
Generate a surface triangulation of the partially rigid nylon and partially flexible PDMS fin.
Use a commercial structural dynamics software to obtain the eigenmodes of the hybrid material.
Perform scaling studies to match the steady-state displacement obtained using uniform pressure differential on the fin surfaces.
Scale the modes to match the displacement obtained from the software.
With the proper scale factor, use the first few dominant modes employed in the coupled FSI solver to simulate unsteady flow over the flexible fin.
Treat the body as an embedded entity in a background mesh.
Prescribe the kinematics of the fin motion from experiments.
Monitor the time history of force production and the shape of the fin along several plane cuts throughout the flapping cycle.
Compare the results with experimental data.
